title.zh: 卷一百十二 列傳第六十二: 李暠 李麟 李國貞 李峘 李巨
title.en: Volume 112 Biographies 62: Li Gao, Li Lin, Li Guozhen, Li Huan, Li Ju
title.raw: 卷一百十二 列傳第六十二: 李暠 李麟 李國貞 李峘 李巨 Volume 112 Biographies 62: Li Gao, Li Lin, Li Guozhen, Li Huan, Li Ju

sentences.zh: 李暠族弟齊物齊物子復暠族弟若水

translations.literal: Li Gao; his clansman younger cousin Qi Wu; Qi Wu's son Fu; Gao's clansman younger cousin Ruoshui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao; his clansman cousin Qi Wu; Qi Wu's son Fu; and Gao's clansman cousin Ruoshui.

sentences.zh: 李麟李國貞子锜

translations.literal: Li Lin; Li Guozhen's son Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lin; and Li Guozhen's son Qi.

sentences.zh: 李峘弟嶧峴

translations.literal: Li Huan; younger brothers Yi and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan; and his younger brothers Yi and Xian.

sentences.zh: 李巨子則之

translations.literal: Li Ju; son Zezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju; and his son Zezhi.

sentences.zh: 李暠，淮安王神通玄孫，清河王孝節孫也。

translations.literal: Li Gao was a great-great-grandson of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and a grandson of Prince Qinghe Li Xiaojie.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao was a great-great-grandson of Prince Huai'an of the Tang, Li Shentong, and a grandson of Prince Qinghe, Li Xiaojie.

sentences.zh: 暠少孤，事母甚謹。

translations.literal: Gao lost his father young and served his mother with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was orphaned early and attended his mother with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 睿宗時，累轉衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: Under Ruizong he was repeatedly transferred and became Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: During Ruizong's reign he rose through several posts to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 丁憂去職，在喪柴毀，家人密親未嘗窺其言笑。

translations.literal: When his mourning obligations began he left office; in mourning he wasted away like dry firewood, and even close kin in the household never caught sight of him speaking or smiling.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning and grew so emaciated in grief that even his household intimates never once saw him speak or smile.

sentences.zh: 開元初，授汝州刺史，為政嚴簡，州境肅然。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was appointed prefect of Ruzhou; his government was stern yet simple, and the prefecture became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he was made prefect of Ruzhou, where his stern but uncluttered rule brought the whole jurisdiction to order.

sentences.zh: 與兄昇弟暈，尤相篤睦，昇等每月自東都省暠，往來微行，州人不之覺，其清慎如此。

translations.literal: With his elder brother Sheng and younger brother Yun he was especially affectionate and harmonious; each month Sheng and the others came from the Eastern Capital to visit Gao, traveling incognito on the road, and the people of the prefecture never noticed—such was his discretion and caution.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially close to his elder brother Sheng and younger brother Yun, who each month traveled from the Eastern Capital to visit him in plain dress so that the people of the prefecture never knew they had come—such was his reputation for discretion.

sentences.zh: 俄入授太常少卿，三遷黃門侍郎，兼太原尹，仍充太原已北諸軍節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he entered the capital and was made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; after three promotions he became Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Metropolitan Governor of Taiyuan, and also served as military commissioner of all armies north of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to court as Vice Minister of Rites, promoted three times to Vice Minister of the Secretariat, and appointed concurrently metropolitan governor of Taiyuan and military commissioner for all forces north of that city.

sentences.zh: 太原舊俗，有僧徒以習禪為業，及死不殮，但以屍送近郊以飼鳥獸。

translations.literal: An old custom of Taiyuan held that certain monks who made meditation their profession, when they died, were not encoffined but only had their corpses taken to the near suburbs to feed birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan it had long been the custom among monks devoted to Chan practice that when they died their bodies were not buried but were carried to the outskirts to be left for birds and wild animals.

sentences.zh: 如是積年，土人號其地為「黃坑」。

translations.literal: This went on for many years, and the local people called the place "Yellow Pit".
translations.idiomatic: Year after year the practice continued, and locals called the place "Yellow Pit".

sentences.zh: 側有餓狗千數，食死人肉，因侵害幼弱，遠近患之，前後官吏不能禁止。

translations.literal: Beside it were several thousand starving dogs that ate the flesh of the dead and thereby preyed on the young and weak; near and far suffered from them, and successive officials could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of starving dogs fed on the corpses and began attacking children; the whole region was troubled by them, yet one official after another had failed to stop it.

sentences.zh: 暠到官，申明禮憲，期不再犯，發兵捕殺群狗，其風遂革。

translations.literal: When Gao took office he proclaimed ritual law and set a term after which the practice must not recur; he sent troops to hunt down and kill the pack of dogs, and the custom was reformed.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao took office he proclaimed the rites and laws, forbade any repetition of the custom, sent troops to destroy the dog packs, and the practice was abolished.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉太常卿，旬日，拜工部尚書、東都留守。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; within ten days he was appointed Minister of Works and Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he became Minister of Rites, and within ten days was appointed Minister of Works and defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 開元二十一年正月，制曰：「繼好之義，雖屬邊鄙；

translations.literal: In the first month of Kaiyuan year 21 an edict said: The duty of continuing friendly relations, though it concerns the borderlands—
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kaiyuan 21 an edict declared: "The duty of sustaining amity, though it belongs to the frontier—

sentences.zh: 受命以出，必在親賢。

translations.literal: when one receives a commission to go forth, it must fall to a kinsman of worth.
translations.idiomatic: when an envoy is commissioned to go abroad, he must be a kinsman of proven worth.

sentences.zh: 事欲重於當時，禮故崇於殊俗，選眾之舉，無出宗英。

translations.literal: the matter must carry weight for the age, and ritual must therefore be exalted toward foreign peoples; in choosing from the multitude, none surpasses a clansman of excellence.
translations.idiomatic: the mission must carry weight in its own time, and ceremony must therefore be elevated toward foreign peoples; in choosing from the many, none surpasses an outstanding member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書李暠，體含柔嘉，識致明允，為公族之領袖，是朝廷之羽儀。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Li Gao embodies gentle excellence; his insight is clear and fair. He is a leader among the imperial kindred and an ornament of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Li Gao is gentle and upright in character, clear and judicious in mind, a leader among the imperial clan and an ornament of the court.

sentences.zh: 金城公主既在蕃中，漢庭公卿非無專對，有懷於遠，夫豈能忘，宜持節充入吐蕃使，準式發遣。」

translations.literal: Since Princess Jincheng is already among the Tibetans, the Han court is not without men able to reply point by point; concern for what lies afar—how could it be forgotten? He should bear credentials as envoy to Tibet and be dispatched according to regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jincheng is already in Tibet, and the Han court has no lack of men fit to answer in detail; concern for distant affairs cannot be set aside. He should go as credentialed envoy to Tibet and be dispatched according to protocol."

sentences.zh: 以國信物一萬匹、私覿物二千匹，皆雜以五彩遣之。

translations.literal: He was sent with ten thousand bolts of state gifts and two thousand bolts of private presentation goods, all mixed in five colors.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent off with ten thousand bolts of state gifts and two thousand bolts of private tribute goods, all woven in five colors.

sentences.zh: 及還，金城公主上言，請以今年九月一日樹碑於赤嶺，定蕃、漢界。

translations.literal: When he returned, Princess Jincheng submitted a memorial asking that on the first day of the ninth month of that year a stele be erected at Chiling to fix the Tibetan and Han border.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Princess Jincheng petitioned that a boundary stele be erected at Red Ridge on the first day of the ninth month to mark the Tibetan and Han frontier.

sentences.zh: 樹碑之日，詔張守珪、李行袆與吐蕃使莽布支同往觀焉。

translations.literal: On the day the stele was set up, Zhang Shougui, Li Xingyi, and the Tibetan envoy Mangbuzhi were ordered to go together to witness it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the stele was raised, Zhang Shougui, Li Xingyi, and the Tibetan envoy Mangbuzhi were ordered to attend together.

sentences.zh: 既而吐蕃遣其臣隨漢使分往劍南及河西、磧西，歷告邊州曰：「兩國和好，無相侵掠。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Tibet sent its officials to follow the Han envoys separately to Jiannan and to Hexi and west of the desert, announcing at each border prefecture: The two states are at peace and shall not encroach on one another."
translations.idiomatic: Tibet then sent officials to accompany the Han envoys to Jiannan, Hexi, and the regions west of the desert, proclaiming at each border prefecture: "The two realms are at peace and shall not attack one another."

sentences.zh: 漢使告亦如之。

translations.literal: The Han envoys made the same proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: The Han envoys proclaimed the same message.

sentences.zh: 以暠奉使稱職，轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Because Gao had fulfilled his mission, he was transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gao had acquitted himself well on the mission, he was made Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時吏部告身印與曹印文同，行用參雜，難以區分，暠奏請準司勛兵部印文例，加「官告」兩字，至今行之。

translations.literal: At that time the Personnel Ministry's commission seal and the bureau seal bore the same inscription; in use they were mixed and hard to distinguish. Gao memorialized that, following the precedent of the Ministry of Personnel for Honors and the Ministry of War seals, the two characters "official commission" be added—a practice followed to this day.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Personnel Ministry's appointment seal matched the bureau seal in its inscription, so the two were easily confused in use. Gao memorialized that, following the practice of the Ministries of Honors and of War, the words "official commission" be added to the seal—a rule still observed today.

sentences.zh: 暠風儀秀整，所歷皆以威重見稱，朝廷稱其有宰相之望。

translations.literal: Gao's bearing was elegant and composed; in every post he was praised for dignity and weight, and the court said he had the makings of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was handsome and dignified in bearing; in every office he was praised for gravity and decorum, and the court regarded him as a man with the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 累封武都縣伯，俄為太子少傅。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Baron of Wudu County and soon became Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Wudu and soon appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 病卒，年六十余，贈益州大都督。

translations.literal: He died of illness at over sixty; posthumously he was made Grand Protector-General of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in his sixties and was posthumously made Grand Protector-General of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 齊物，淮安王神通子、鹽州刺史銳孫也。

translations.literal: Qi Wu was a son of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and a grandson of Salt Prefecture Governor Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wu was a son of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and a grandson of the Salt Prefecture governor Rui.

sentences.zh: 齊物無學術，在官嚴整。

translations.literal: Qi Wu had no scholarly learning but was stern and orderly in office.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wu was not a man of learning, but he was stern and exacting in office.

sentences.zh: 開元二十四年後，歷懷、陜二州刺史。

translations.literal: After Kaiyuan year 24 he served in succession as prefect of Huai and Shan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After Kaiyuan 24 he served successively as prefect of Huai and Shan.

sentences.zh: 齊物天寶初開砥柱之險，以通流運，於石中得古鐵犁鏵，有「平陸」字，因改河北縣為平陸縣，加齊物銀青光祿大夫，為鴻臚卿、河南尹。

translations.literal: Early in Tianbao, Qi Wu opened the perilous narrows at Dizhu to allow transport by water; in the rock he found an ancient iron plowshare bearing the characters Pinglu, and therefore renamed Hebei County as Pinglu County. Qi Wu was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and made Minister of Ceremonial and Metropolitan Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao, Qi Wu cleared the dangerous Dizhu narrows to open river transport; in the rock he found an ancient iron plowshare inscribed "Pinglu," and renamed Hebei County Pinglu. He was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and appointed Minister of Ceremonial and metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 齊物與右相李適之善，適之為林甫所構貶官，齊物坐謫竟陵太守。

translations.literal: Qi Wu was on good terms with the Right Chancellor Li Shizhi; when Shizhi was framed by Li Linfu and demoted, Qi Wu was implicated and banished as prefect of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wu was close to Right Chancellor Li Shizhi; when Shizhi was framed by Li Linfu and demoted, Qi Wu was implicated and exiled as prefect of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 入為司農、鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of Agriculture and Minister of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Minister of Agriculture and Minister of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 至德初，拜太子賓客，遷刑部尚書、鳳翔尹、太常卿、京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide he was made Guest of the Heir Apparent, then transferred to Minister of Justice, Metropolitan Governor of Fengxiang, Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhide he became a guest of the heir apparent, then Minister of Justice, metropolitan governor of Fengxiang, Minister of Rites, and metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 為政發官吏陰事，以察為能，於物少恩，而清廉自飭，人吏莫敢抵犯。

translations.literal: In government he exposed officials' hidden affairs and took keen scrutiny as his talent; toward others he showed little kindness, yet he kept himself pure and restrained, and neither people nor clerks dared oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed by exposing officials' secret misconduct and prided himself on sharp scrutiny; he showed little mercy toward others, yet kept himself scrupulously honest, and neither people nor clerks dared cross him.

sentences.zh: 晚年除太子太傅、兼宗正卿。

translations.literal: In his later years he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 上元二年五月卒，輟朝一日。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth month of Shangyuan year 2; court audiences were suspended for one day.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of Shangyuan 2, and court audiences were suspended for a day.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「故金紫光祿大夫、太子太傅、兼宗正卿齊物，宗室珪璋，士林楨幹，清廉獨斷，剛毅不群。

translations.literal: An edict said: The late Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal Qi Wu, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan Court, was a jade tablet of the imperial house and a pillar of the scholarly world—pure, independent in judgment, resolute and standing apart from the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The late Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal Qi Wu, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently director of the Imperial Clan Court, was a jewel of the imperial house and a pillar of the scholarly world—upright, decisive, firm, and unlike ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 歷踐周行，備經中外，威名益振，忠效彌彰。

translations.literal: He trod the full circuit of offices and served both within and beyond the capital; his renown for authority grew ever greater and his loyal service ever clearer.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through the full round of offices at court and in the provinces; his reputation for authority grew ever stronger and his loyal service ever clearer.

sentences.zh: 三尹神州，一登會府，擒奸掩鉤距之術，恤獄正喉舌之官。

translations.literal: Three times he governed the sacred capital; once he rose to the metropolitan office. He seized traitors and mastered the arts of entrapment; he showed compassion in prisons and rectified the office of the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he governed the imperial capital, once he held high metropolitan office, he mastered the arts of exposing wrongdoing, showed compassion in the prisons, and set right the censorial office.

sentences.zh: 遂令調護儲闈，再登師傅，從容賓友，師長官僚。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to attend the heir's quarters, twice rose as tutor, served as a composed companion, and guided the official corps.
translations.idiomatic: He was then charged with the care of the heir's household, twice served as tutor, was a steady companion to the throne, and guided the official ranks.

sentences.zh: 桑榆之時，壯誌逾勵；

translations.literal: In the evening of life his great resolve only grew keener;
translations.idiomatic: In the twilight of his years his high resolve only grew keener;

sentences.zh: 松柏之性，晚歲常堅。

translations.literal: the nature of pine and cypress remained firm in late age.
translations.idiomatic: like pine and cypress, he stood firm to the end.

sentences.zh: 天不慭遺，奄然殂謝，念親感舊，深軫於懷。

translations.literal: Heaven was not kind in leaving him; suddenly he passed away. Remembering a kinsman and moved by an old friend, We are deeply stricken in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven was not kind to leave him; he has suddenly departed. Thinking of a kinsman and an old servant of the state, We are deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 宜錫寵章，載光營魄。

translations.literal: He should be granted favor in edict and his spirit honored in glory.
translations.idiomatic: Let honors be bestowed upon him and his spirit illumined in death.

sentences.zh: 可贈太子太師。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent."
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent."

sentences.zh: 子復，字初陽，以父廕累官至江陵府司錄。

translations.literal: Zi Fu, style name Chuyang, through his father's privilege rose in office to Registrar of Jiangling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, styled Chuyang, rose through his father's privilege to registrar of Jiangling prefecture.

sentences.zh: 精曉吏道，衛伯玉厚遇之，府中之事，多以咨委。

translations.literal: He was thoroughly versed in administrative practice; Wei Boyu treated him generously and entrusted him with most affairs of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was expert in administrative practice; Wei Boyu treated him well and entrusted him with most of the prefecture's business.

sentences.zh: 性苛刻，為伯玉所信，奏為江陵縣令，遷少尹，歷饒州、蘇州刺史，皆著政聲。

translations.literal: His nature was harsh; Boyu trusted him and memorialized him as magistrate of Jiangling County; he was promoted to Vice Governor and served as prefect of Raozhou and Suzhou, winning a reputation for good government in each.
translations.idiomatic: He was harsh by nature but trusted by Boyu, who recommended him as magistrate of Jiangling county; he was promoted to vice governor and later served as prefect of Raozhou and Suzhou, earning a reputation for good government in each post.

sentences.zh: 李希烈背叛，荊南節度張伯儀數出兵，為希烈所敗，朝廷憂之。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie rebelled, Jingnan military commissioner Zhang Boyi repeatedly took the field and was defeated by Xilie; the court was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled, the Jingnan commissioner Zhang Boyi led several campaigns and was repeatedly defeated; the court was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 以復久在江陵，得軍民心，復方在母喪，起為江陵少尹、兼御史中丞，充節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Because Fu had long been at Jiangling and had won the hearts of soldiers and people, though he was in mourning for his mother he was recalled as Vice Governor of Jiangling and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, serving as campaigning deputy of the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fu had long served at Jiangling and had won the loyalty of troops and people, he was recalled from mourning for his mother as vice governor of Jiangling and vice censor-in-chief, and made campaigning deputy of the military commission.

sentences.zh: 伯儀既受代，以復為容州刺史、兼御史中丞，充本管招討使，加檢校常侍。

translations.literal: After Boyi was replaced, Fu was made prefect of Rongzhou and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, serving as pacification commissioner of the circuit, with the added title of irregularly appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Boyi was relieved, Fu was made prefect of Rongzhou and vice censor-in-chief, appointed pacification commissioner of the circuit, and given the added title of irregular palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 先時西原叛亂，前後經略使征討反者，獲其人皆沒為官奴婢，配作坊重役，復乃令訪其親屬，悉歸還之。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the Xiyuan rebellion, successive frontier commissioners who campaigned against rebels had all captives made state slaves and assigned to workshops for heavy labor. Fu ordered their kin sought out and all returned to them.
translations.idiomatic: During the earlier Xiyuan rebellion, successive frontier commissioners had enslaved captured rebels and sent them to workshops for hard labor; Fu ordered their kin traced and all such captives restored to their families.

sentences.zh: 在容州三歲，南人安悅。

translations.literal: After three years at Rongzhou the southern peoples were content.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in Rongzhou the southern peoples were at peace.

sentences.zh: 遷廣州刺史、兼御史大夫、嶺南節度觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Guangzhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and military commissioner and observation commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Guangzhou, censor-in-chief, and military and observation commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 會安南經略使高正平、張應相次卒官，其下參佐偏裨李元度、胡懷義等阻兵，黷亂州縣，奸贓狼藉。

translations.literal: It happened that the Annan frontier commissioners Gao Zhengping and Zhang Ying died in office one after another; their subordinate staff officers and commanders Li Yuandu, Hu Huaiyi, and others held troops in defiance, ravaged prefectures and counties, and left corruption in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: When the Annan commissioners Gao Zhengping and Zhang Ying died in succession, their subordinates Li Yuandu, Hu Huaiyi, and others kept troops under arms, ravaged the prefectures and counties, and spread corruption everywhere.

sentences.zh: 復誘懷義杖殺之，奏元度流於荒裔。

translations.literal: Fu induced Huaiyi to beat one man to death with the staff and memorialized that Yuandu be exiled to the remote border.
translations.idiomatic: Fu induced Hu Huaiyi to have one of them beaten to death, then memorialized that Li Yuandu be exiled to the far frontier.

sentences.zh: 又勸導百姓，令變茅屋為瓦舍。

translations.literal: He also urged and guided the people to change thatched huts into tiled houses.
translations.idiomatic: He also encouraged the people to replace thatched huts with tiled houses.

sentences.zh: 瓊州久陷於蠻獠中，復累遣使喻之，因奏置瓊州都督府以綏撫之。

translations.literal: Qiongzhou had long been lost among the Man and Liao; Fu repeatedly sent envoys to instruct them and memorialized to establish the Qiongzhou Protectorate to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiongzhou had long been overrun by tribal peoples; Fu sent envoys again and again to win them over and memorialized for the establishment of a Qiongzhou protectorate to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 復曉於政道，所在稱理，征拜宗正卿，加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: Fu understood the way of government; wherever he served he was praised for good order. He was summoned as Director of the Imperial Clan Court and given the added post of irregularly appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Fu understood governance well and was praised for good order wherever he served; he was summoned as director of the Imperial Clan Court with the added title of irregular Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 未一歲，會華州節度李元諒卒，以復為華州刺史、潼關防禦鎮國軍使，仍檢校戶部尚書，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Within less than a year, when Huazhou military commissioner Li Yuanliang died, Fu was made prefect of Huazhou, defender of Tong Pass and commissioner of the Zhenguo Army, while retaining the irregular post of Minister of Revenue and concurrently serving as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year, when the Huazhou commissioner Li Yuanliang died, Fu was made prefect of Huazhou, defender of Tong Pass and commander of the Zhenguo army, while retaining the irregular post of Minister of Revenue and serving concurrently as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年，鄭滑節度使李融卒，軍中潰亂，以復檢校兵部尚書，兼滑州刺史、義成軍節度、鄭滑觀察營田等使、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan year 10 the Zheng-Hua military commissioner Li Rong died and the army fell into disorder; Fu was made irregularly appointed Minister of War, concurrently prefect of Huazhou, military commissioner of the Yicheng Army, observation and garrison-farm commissioner of Zheng-Hua, and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 10 the Zheng-Hua commissioner Li Rong died and the army fell into disorder; Fu was appointed irregular Minister of War, prefect of Huazhou, military commissioner of the Yicheng army, Zheng-Hua observation and garrison-farm commissioner, and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 復到任，置營田數百頃，以資軍食，不率於民，眾皆悅之。

translations.literal: When Fu took office he established several hundred qing of garrison farms to supply the army's food without levying on the people, and all were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he established several hundred qing of garrison farms to supply the army without taxing the people, and won wide approval.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: In year 12 he was given the added title of irregularly appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was given the added title of irregular Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月卒官，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of year 13 he died in office at fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the fourth month of year 13, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，贈司空。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended for three days; posthumously he was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for three days, and he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 賻布帛米粟有差。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts of cloth, silk, grain, and millet were granted in due measure.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral gifts of cloth, silk, grain, and millet were granted in due measure.

sentences.zh: 復久典方面，積財頗甚，為時所譏。

translations.literal: Fu had long governed frontier regions and amassed considerable wealth, for which his contemporaries criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had long governed frontier regions and amassed considerable wealth, for which his contemporaries criticized him.

sentences.zh: 若水，齊物族弟，累官至左金吾大將軍，兼通事舍人。

translations.literal: Ruoshui was Qi Wu's clansman cousin. He rose through repeated promotions to General of the Left Golden Guards and was concurrently Attendant for Diplomatic Correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui was Qi Wu's clansman cousin. He rose through repeated promotions to General of the Left Golden Guards and was concurrently Attendant for Diplomatic Correspondence.

sentences.zh: 容貌甚偉，在館三十年，多識舊儀，每宣勞贊導，周旋俯仰，有可觀者。

translations.literal: His appearance was very imposing. He spent thirty years in the hostel, knew many old protocols, and whenever he announced congratulations and guided ceremonies, his turning and bowing were something worth watching.
translations.idiomatic: His appearance was very imposing. He spent thirty years in the hostel, knew many old protocols, and whenever he announced congratulations and guided ceremonies, his turning and bowing were something worth watching.

sentences.zh: 建中元年八月卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth month of Jianzhong 1.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of Jianzhong 1.

sentences.zh: 李麟，皇室之疏屬，太宗之從孫也。

translations.literal: Li Lin was a distant member of the imperial house, a collateral descendant of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lin was a distant kinsman of the imperial house, a collateral descendant of Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 父浚，開元初置十道按察使，精選吏才，以浚為潤州刺史、江南東道按察使。

translations.literal: His father Jun, when at the beginning of Kaiyuan the ten-circuit investigation commissioners were established and able officials were carefully chosen, was made prefect of Runzhou and investigation commissioner of Jiangnan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun, when the ten-circuit investigation commissioners were established early in Kaiyuan and able officials were carefully selected, was made prefect of Runzhou and investigation commissioner of Jiangnan East.

sentences.zh: 轉虢潞二州刺史，益州大都督府長史、攝御史大夫、劍南節度按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Guo and Lu prefectures, then chief administrator of the Yizhou Grand Protectorate, acting Censor-in-Chief, and investigation commissioner of the Jiannan military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Guo and Lu, then chief administrator of the Yizhou protectorate, acting censor-in-chief, and investigation commissioner of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 所歷以誠信待物，稱為良吏。

translations.literal: In every post he treated others with sincerity and trust and was called a good official.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he dealt with others in good faith and was regarded as an excellent official.

sentences.zh: 八年卒，贈戶部尚書，謚曰誠。

translations.literal: He died in year 8; posthumously he was made Minister of Revenue, with the posthumous title Sincere.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 8 and was posthumously made Minister of Revenue with the posthumous title Sincere.

sentences.zh: 麟以父任補職，累授京兆府戶曹。

translations.literal: Lin entered office through his father's privilege and was repeatedly appointed Registrar of Revenue in Jingzhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lin entered office through his father's privilege and rose to registrar of revenue in Jingzhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開元二十二年，舉宗室異能，轉殿中侍御史，歷戶部、考功、吏部三員外郎。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan year 22 he was recommended for unusual ability among the imperial clan, transferred to Attending Censor within the Palace, and served as vice director in the Ministries of Revenue, Honors, and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 22 he was recommended for unusual ability among the imperial clan, became an attending censor within the palace, and served as vice director in the ministries of Revenue, Honors, and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，遷郎中，尋改諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In Tianbao year 1 he was promoted to director; soon after he was made Grand Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 he was promoted to director and soon made grand adviser.

sentences.zh: 五載，充河西、隴右、磧西等道黜陟使，稱旨，遷給事中。

translations.literal: In year 5 he served as promotion-and-demotion commissioner for Hexi, Longyou, and the regions west of the desert; he pleased the throne and was made Supervisor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he served as promotion-and-demotion commissioner for Hexi, Longyou, and the regions west of the desert; he pleased the emperor and was made supervisor of the palace.

sentences.zh: 七載，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In year 7 he was made Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he became Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 同列楊國忠專權，不悅麟同職，宰臣奏麟以本官權知禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: His colleague Yang Guozhong monopolized power and disliked sharing rank with Lin; the chief ministers memorialized that Lin, in his present office, should act as temporary director of the Ministry of Rites examinations.
translations.idiomatic: His colleague Yang Guozhong held sole power and disliked sharing rank with Lin; the chief ministers memorialized that Lin be given temporary charge of the Ministry of Rites examinations.

sentences.zh: 俄而國忠為御史大夫，麟復本官。

translations.literal: Soon Guozhong became Censor-in-Chief and Lin returned to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozhong soon became censor-in-chief, Lin returned to his original post.

sentences.zh: 十一載，遷銀青光祿大夫、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In year 11 he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 十四年七月，以本官出為河東太守、河東道采訪使，為政清簡，民吏稱之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of year 14 he left the capital in his present rank as prefect of Hedong and investigation commissioner of Hedong Circuit; his government was pure and simple, and people and officials praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 14 he went out as prefect of Hedong and investigation commissioner of Hedong circuit; his rule was plain and orderly, and both people and officials praised him.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，祿山構逆，朝廷以麟儒者，恐非禦侮之用，仍以將軍呂崇賁代還。

translations.literal: That winter Lushan plotted rebellion; the court considered Lin a scholar and feared he was not fit to repel invasion, and sent General Lü Chongben to replace him and recall him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter when Lushan rebelled, the court regarded Lin as a scholar unlikely to meet the needs of defense and sent General Lü Chongben to replace him and recall him.

sentences.zh: 復以祭酒歸朝，賜爵渭源縣男。

translations.literal: He returned to court again as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and was enfeoffed as Baron of Weiyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as chancellor of the Directorate of Education and was enfeoffed as Baron of Weiyuan.

sentences.zh: 六月，玄宗幸蜀，麟奔赴行在。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Xuanzong went to Shu; Lin hurried to the imperial headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, when Xuanzong went to Shu, Lin hurried to join the imperial headquarters.

sentences.zh: 既至成都，拜戶部侍郎，兼左丞。

translations.literal: When he reached Chengdu he was made Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Chengdu he was made Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently left vice director.

sentences.zh: 遷憲部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 至德二年正月，拜同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the first month of Zhide year 2 he was made Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhide 2 he was appointed associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 時扈從宰相韋見素、房琯、崔渙已赴鳳翔，俄而崔圓繼去，玄宗以麟宗室子，獨留之，行在百司，麟總攝其事。

translations.literal: At that time the accompanying chancellors Wei Jiansu, Fang Guan, and Cui Huan had already gone to Fengxiang; soon Cui Yuan followed. Xuanzong, because Lin was of the imperial clan, kept him alone; of the hundred offices at the headquarters, Lin took overall charge of their affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By then the accompanying chancellors Wei Jiansu, Fang Guan, and Cui Huan had already gone to Fengxiang, and Cui Yuan soon followed. Xuanzong kept Lin alone because he was of the imperial clan, and Lin took charge of all the offices at the imperial headquarters.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，從上皇還京，策勛行賞，加金紫光祿大夫、刑部尚書、同中書門下三品，進封褒國公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year he followed the Retired Emperor back to the capital; merits were assessed and rewards given. He was given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal, Minister of Justice, and Third Rank under the Secretariat and Chancellery, and advanced to Duke of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year he followed the retired emperor back to the capital; when merits were rewarded he was given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal, Minister of Justice, and third rank under the Secretariat, and advanced to Duke of Bao.

sentences.zh: 時張皇后干預朝政，殿中監李輔國以翊衛肅宗之勞，判天下兵馬事，充元帥府行軍司馬，勢傾同朝。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Zhang intervened in court affairs. Director of the Palace Domestic Service Li Fuguo, for his service escorting Suzong, was made commander of all military affairs under heaven, served as Chief of Staff of the Marshal's headquarters, and his power dominated the court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Zhang intervened in court affairs. Li Fuguo, Director of the Palace Domestic Service, for escorting Suzong was made commander of all military affairs under heaven and Chief of Staff of the Marshal's headquarters, and his power dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 宰相苗晉卿、崔圓已下懼其威權，傾心事之，唯麟正身謹事，無所依附，輔國不悅。

translations.literal: The chancellors Miao Jingqing, Cui Yuan, and all below feared his authority and devoted themselves to him; only Lin served with upright caution and attached himself to no one, and Fuguo was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Miao Jingqing, Cui Yuan, and all below feared his authority and courted him; only Lin served with upright caution and attached himself to no one, and Fuguo was displeased.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，罷麟知政事，守太子少傅。

translations.literal: In Qianyuan 1 Lin was removed from handling administration and kept on as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 1 Lin was removed from handling administration and kept on as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年八月卒，時年六十六，贈太子太傅，賻絹二百匹。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of year 2 he died at the age of sixty-six; he was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with two hundred bolts of silk as funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 2 he died at sixty-six; he was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with two hundred bolts of silk as funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 葬日，詔京兆府差官護送，官給所須。

translations.literal: On the day of burial an edict ordered Jingzhao prefecture to assign officials to escort the funeral and supply all that was needed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial an edict ordered Jingzhao prefecture to assign officials to escort the funeral and supply all that was needed.

sentences.zh: 麟好學能文，嘗編聚皇朝已來制集五十卷，行於時。

translations.literal: Lin loved learning and was skilled in letters; he once compiled a collection of fifty juan of regulations from the imperial house to his day, which circulated at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Lin loved learning and was skilled in letters; he once compiled a fifty-juan collection of regulations from the imperial house to his day, which circulated at the time.

sentences.zh: 李國貞，淮安王神通子、淄川王孝同之曾孫。

translations.literal: Li Guozhen was a son of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and a great-grandson of Prince Zichuan Li Xiaotong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guozhen was a son of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and a great-grandson of Prince Zichuan Li Xiaotong.

sentences.zh: 父廣業，劍州長史。

translations.literal: His father Guangye was chief administrator of Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangye was chief administrator of Jian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 國貞本名若幽，性剛正，有吏才，歷安定、扶風錄事參軍，皆稱職。

translations.literal: Guozhen's original name was Ruoyou. His nature was upright and firm; he had talent for administration. He served as recording secretary in Anding and Fufeng and in each was praised as competent.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's original name was Ruoyou. He was upright and firm by nature and had administrative talent; he served as recording secretary in Anding and Fufeng and was praised as competent in both.

sentences.zh: 乾元中累遷長安令，尋拜河南尹。

translations.literal: In the Qianyuan era he was repeatedly promoted to magistrate of Chang'an and soon made Metropolitan Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyuan he rose to magistrate of Chang'an and soon became metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 會史思明逼城，元帥李光弼東保河陽，國貞領官吏寓於陜。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming pressed the city, the commander Li Guangbi withdrew east to secure Heyang; Guozhen led officials and clerks to lodge at Shan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming besieged the city, the commander Li Guangbi withdrew east to hold Heyang, and Guozhen led the officials to take refuge at Shan.

sentences.zh: 數月，征為京兆尹。

translations.literal: After several months he was summoned as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was summoned to be metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 上元初，改成都尹、兼御史大夫，充劍南節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan he was changed to Metropolitan Governor of Chengdu and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, serving as military commissioner of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shangyuan he was made metropolitan governor of Chengdu and censor-in-chief, and military commissioner of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 入為殿中監。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as director of the palace domestic service.

sentences.zh: 二年八月，遷戶部尚書、兼御史大夫，持節充朔方、鎮西、北庭、興平、陳鄭等節度行營兵馬及河中節度都統處置使，鎮於絳，賜名國貞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of year 2 he was made Minister of Revenue and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, bearing credentials as commander of the campaigning forces of the Shuo-fang, Zhenxi, Beiting, Xingping, Chen-Zheng, and other military commissions and as overall commander and disposal commissioner of the Hezhong commission, stationed at Jiang; he was granted the name Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 2 he became Minister of Revenue and censor-in-chief, with credentials as commander of the campaigning forces of Shuo-fang, Zhenxi, Beiting, Xingping, Chen-Zheng, and other commissions and as overall commander of Hezhong; he was stationed at Jiang and granted the name Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 既至，又加充管內河中、晉、絳、慈、隰、沁等州觀察處置等使，余並如故。

translations.literal: When he arrived he was further made observation and disposal commissioner for Hezhong, Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, Qin, and other prefectures within his jurisdiction; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was also made observation and disposal commissioner for Hezhong, Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, Qin, and the other prefectures under his command; his other titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 國貞既至絳，屬軍中素無儲積，百姓饑饉，難為聚斂，將士等糧賜多闕。

translations.literal: When Guozhen reached Jiang, the army had long had no stores, the people were suffering famine, and levies were hard to collect; officers and soldiers were often short of grain rations and stipends.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozhen reached Jiang, the army had no reserves, the people were starving, and levies were hard to raise; officers and soldiers were often short of rations and pay.

sentences.zh: 國貞頻以狀聞，未報。

translations.literal: Guozhen repeatedly reported the situation but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen reported the situation again and again but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 軍中喧喧怨讀，左右以告國貞，國貞喻之曰：「軍將何苦如是，已為奏聞，終有所給。」

translations.literal: The army grew noisy with resentment; his attendants told Guozhen, and Guozhen explained to them: Why must you officers suffer so? I have already memorialized the court; in the end there will be provisions."
translations.idiomatic: The army grew loud with complaint; when his attendants told him, Guozhen reassured them: "Why must you officers suffer so? I have already memorialized the court, and supplies will come in the end."

sentences.zh: 信宿軍亂，攻國貞，夜燒衙城門。

translations.literal: Within two nights the army mutinied, attacked Guozhen, and burned the yamen city gate by night.
translations.idiomatic: Within two nights the army mutinied, attacked Guozhen, and burned the yamen gate by night.

sentences.zh: 國貞莫知所圖，左右勸國貞棄城遁去，國貞曰：「吾銜命為將，不能靖難，安可棄城乎！」

translations.literal: Guozhen did not know what they intended; his attendants urged him to abandon the city and flee. Guozhen said: I received a commission as a general; if I cannot quell disorder, how can I abandon the city!"
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen did not know what they meant; his attendants urged him to abandon the city and flee. He said: "I was commissioned as a general; if I cannot quell disorder, how can I abandon the city!"

sentences.zh: 左右固勸回避，乃隱於州獄，詐負縲紲。

translations.literal: His attendants pressed him to withdraw, so he hid in the prefectural prison and pretended to wear fetters.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants pressed him to hide, so he concealed himself in the prefectural prison and pretended to be in chains.

sentences.zh: 會國貞麾下為賊所擒，因指所在，遂於獄中執國貞，將害之，國貞曰：「軍中乏糧，已有陳請，人不堪賦，予無負於將士耳。」

translations.literal: It happened that one of Guozhen's subordinates was seized by the mutineers and pointed out where he was; they then seized Guozhen in the prison and were about to kill him. Guozhen said: The army lacks grain; I have already submitted a request. The people cannot bear more levies; I have done no wrong to you officers and soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: One of his subordinates was captured by the mutineers and revealed his hiding place; they seized him in the prison and were about to kill him. Guozhen said: "The army lacks grain and I have already petitioned the court. The people cannot bear more levies; I have done you officers and soldiers no wrong."

sentences.zh: 眾引退。

translations.literal: The crowd withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd withdrew.

sentences.zh: 突將王元振獨曰：「今日之事，豈須問焉！」

translations.literal: The assault officer Wang Yuanzhen alone said: For today's affair, is there any need to ask!"
translations.idiomatic: The assault officer Wang Yuanzhen alone cried: "For today's business, is there any need to ask!"

sentences.zh: 抽刀害國貞及二男、三大將。

translations.literal: He drew his blade and killed Guozhen, his two sons, and three great generals.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his blade and killed Guozhen, his two sons, and three senior generals.

sentences.zh: 國貞有風采，清白守法，為政急於操下，時論以辨吏稱之。

translations.literal: Guozhen had presence and bearing, kept himself pure and observed the law, and in government was severe in controlling subordinates; contemporary opinion praised him as a discerning official.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen was a man of presence, upright and law-abiding, severe toward subordinates in office, and was praised by his contemporaries as a discerning administrator.

sentences.zh: 追贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Grand Protector-General of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Protector-General of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子锜，以父廕貞元中累至湖、杭二州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Qi, through his father's privilege, rose in the Zhenyuan era to prefect of Hu and Hang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi, through his father's privilege, rose during Zhenyuan to prefect of Hu and Hang.

sentences.zh: 多以寶貨賂李齊運，由是遷潤州刺史兼鹽鐵使，持積財進奉，以結恩澤，德宗甚寵之。

translations.literal: He gave many treasures in bribes to Li Qiyun and thereby was transferred to prefect of Runzhou and concurrently Salt and Iron Commissioner; he used accumulated wealth in tribute offerings to win favor, and Dezong greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: He bribed Li Qiyun with many treasures and was transferred to prefect of Runzhou and salt and iron commissioner; he sent up accumulated wealth as tribute to win favor, and Dezong greatly favored him.

sentences.zh: 锜恃恩驕恣，有浙西人布衣崔善貞詣闕上封，論锜罪狀，而德宗械送賜锜，锜遂坑殺善貞，天下切齒。

translations.literal: Qi relied on favor and was arrogant and unrestrained. A commoner of western Zhejiang named Cui Shanzhen went to the capital and submitted a sealed memorial detailing Qi's crimes, but Dezong had him shackled and sent as a gift to Qi; Qi then had Shanzhen buried alive, and all under heaven gnashed their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Qi grew arrogant on imperial favor. A commoner of western Zhejiang, Cui Shanzhen, went to court with a sealed memorial listing Qi's crimes, but Dezong had him shackled and sent to Qi as a gift; Qi had him buried alive, and the whole realm seethed with hatred.

sentences.zh: 乃增置兵額，選善弓矢者聚之一營，名曰「挽硬隨身」；

translations.literal: He then increased the troop quota and gathered skilled archers in one camp, called the "Hard-Drawing Personal Guard";
translations.idiomatic: He then increased his troop quota and gathered skilled archers in one camp called the "Hard-Drawing Personal Guard";

sentences.zh: 以胡、奚雜類虬須者為一將，名曰「蕃落健兒」。

translations.literal: he made men of mixed Hu and Xi stock with bristling beards into one command, called the "Tribal Frontier Braves".
translations.idiomatic: and formed another command of mixed Hu and Xi men with bristling beards called the "Tribal Frontier Braves".

sentences.zh: 德宗復於潤州置鎮海軍，以锜為節度使，罷其鹽鐵使務。

translations.literal: Dezong again established the Zhenhai Army at Runzhou, made Qi its military commissioner, and removed him from the salt and iron commission.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong then established the Zhenhai army at Runzhou, made Qi its military commissioner, and removed him from the salt and iron commission.

sentences.zh: 锜雖罷其利權，且得節度，反狀未發。

translations.literal: Although Qi lost his profit-making power, he still gained a military commission, and his rebellion had not yet broken out.
translations.idiomatic: Though Qi lost his lucrative post, he still held a military commission, and his rebellion had not yet broken out.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位已二年，諸道倔強者入朝，而锜不自安，亦請入朝，乃拜锜左僕射。

translations.literal: Two years after Xianzong took the throne, the stubborn military commissioners of the circuits came to court; Qi felt uneasy and also asked to come to court, and was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Two years after Xianzong's accession, the stubborn commissioners came to court; Qi, uneasy, also asked to attend court and was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 锜乃署判官王淡為留後。

translations.literal: Qi then appointed his aide Wang Dan as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Qi appointed his aide Wang Dan acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既而遷延發期，淡與中使頻喻之，不悅，遂諷將士以給冬衣日殺淡而食之。

translations.literal: He then delayed his departure; Dan and the court envoy repeatedly urged him, which displeased him, so he incited the soldiers on the day winter clothing was issued to kill Dan and eat his flesh.
translations.idiomatic: He then delayed his departure; when Dan and the court envoy urged him repeatedly he grew angry and incited the soldiers, on the day winter clothing was issued, to kill Dan and eat his flesh.

sentences.zh: 監軍使聞亂，遣衙將趙锜慰喻，又臠食之。

translations.literal: The army supervisor heard of the disorder and sent the yamen officer Zhao Qi to reassure them; he too was cut up and eaten.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor heard of the mutiny and sent the yamen officer Zhao Qi to calm them; he too was cut up and eaten.

sentences.zh: 復以兵註中使之頸，锜佯驚救解之，囚於別館。

translations.literal: They again held blades to the envoy's neck; Qi pretended to be startled and had him rescued, then imprisoned him in a separate lodge.
translations.idiomatic: They again held blades to the envoy's neck; Qi feigned alarm, had him rescued, and imprisoned him in a separate lodge.

sentences.zh: 遂稱兵，飾五劍，分授管內鎮將，令殺刺史。

translations.literal: He then raised troops, had five swords decorated, and distributed them to the garrison generals within his jurisdiction, ordering them to kill the prefects.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised troops, had five swords decorated, and gave them to the garrison generals under his command with orders to kill the prefects.

sentences.zh: 於是常州刺史顏防用客李雲謀，矯制傳檄於蘇、杭、湖、睦等州，遂殺其鎮將李深；

translations.literal: Thereupon the prefect of Changzhou Yan Fang, using the plan of his client Li Yun, forged an edict and circulated a proclamation to Suzhou, Hangzhou, Huzhou, Mu, and other prefectures, and killed the garrison general Li Shen;
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Changzhou, Yan Fang, using a plan from his client Li Yun, forged an edict and sent proclamations to Suzhou, Hangzhou, Huzhou, Mu, and other prefectures, and killed the garrison general Li Shen;

sentences.zh: 湖州辛秘亦殺其鎮將趙惟忠；

translations.literal: Xin Mi of Huzhou also killed the garrison general Zhao Weizhong;
translations.idiomatic: Xin Mi of Huzhou also killed the garrison general Zhao Weizhong;

sentences.zh: 而蘇州刺史李素為鎮將姚誌安所系，釘於船舷，生致於锜，未至而锜敗，得免。

translations.literal: while the prefect of Suzhou Li Su was bound by the garrison general Yao Zhi'an, nailed to the ship's side, and sent alive to Qi; before he arrived Qi was defeated, and Su escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: while the prefect of Suzhou, Li Su, was bound by the garrison general Yao Zhi'an, nailed to a ship's side, and sent alive to Qi; before he arrived Qi was defeated, and Su was spared.

sentences.zh: 初，锜以宣州富饒，有並吞之意，遣兵馬使張子良、李奉仙、田少卿領兵三千分略宣、池等州。

translations.literal: Earlier Qi, because Xuanzhou was rich, had intended to swallow it up; he sent the military aides Zhang Ziliang, Li Fengxian, and Tian Shaoqing to lead three thousand men in separate attacks on Xuan, Chi, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Xuanzhou was wealthy, Qi had intended to seize it and sent the military aides Zhang Ziliang, Li Fengxian, and Tian Shaoqing with three thousand men to overrun Xuan, Chi, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 三將夙有向順誌，而锜甥裴行立亦思向順，其密謀多決於行立，乃回戈趣城，執锜於幕，縋而出之，斬於闕下，年六十七。

translations.literal: The three generals had long wished to submit to the court, and Qi's nephew Pei Xingli also wished to turn loyal; their secret plans were largely decided by Xingli. They turned their spears back toward the city, seized Qi in his tent, lowered him by rope, and beheaded him below the gate; he was sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The three generals had long wished to submit, and Qi's nephew Pei Xingli also favored loyalty; their secret plans were largely settled by Xingli. They turned back toward the city, seized Qi in his tent, lowered him by rope, and beheaded him before the gate at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 其「挽硬」、「蕃落」將士，或投井自縊，紛紛枕藉而死者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: His "Hard-Drawing" and "Tribal Frontier" soldiers threw themselves into wells or hanged themselves; those who lay dead in heaps were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: His "Hard-Drawing" and "Tribal Frontier" soldiers threw themselves into wells or hanged themselves; the dead lay heaped beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 宰相鄭絪等議锜所坐，親疏未定，乃召兵部郎中蔣武問曰：「詔罪李锜一房，當是大功內耶？」

translations.literal: The chancellor Zheng Yin and others debated the degree of kinship implicated in Qi's crime, which was not yet settled; they summoned Jiang Wu, director in the Ministry of War, and asked: In punishing the household of Li Qi by edict, should that fall within the great-achievement degree of mourning?"
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor Zheng Yin and others debated how far Qi's kin should be punished; they summoned Jiang Wu of the Ministry of War and asked: "In punishing Li Qi's household by edict, should that fall within the great-achievement degree of mourning?"

sentences.zh: 武曰：「大功是锜堂兄弟，即淮安王神通之下，淮安有大功於國，不可以孽孫而上累。」

translations.literal: Wu said: The great-achievement degree covers Qi's cousins, that is, the line below Prince Huai'an Li Shentong. Huai'an rendered great service to the state; one cannot let a guilty descendant implicate his superiors."
translations.idiomatic: Wu said: "The great-achievement degree covers Qi's cousins, the line below Prince Huai'an Li Shentong. Huai'an rendered great service to the state; a guilty descendant must not drag his superiors down with him."

sentences.zh: 又問：「锜親兄弟從坐否？」

translations.literal: They asked again: Should Qi's full brothers share punishment?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked again: "Should Qi's full brothers share punishment?"

sentences.zh: 武曰：「锜親兄弟是若幽之子，若幽有死王事之功，如令锜兄弟從坐，若幽即宜削籍，亦所未安。」

translations.literal: Wu said: Qi's full brothers are sons of Ruoyou. Ruoyou died in service to the throne. If Qi's brothers are punished with him, Ruoyou ought to be struck from the rolls, which would also be unsettling."
translations.idiomatic: Wu said: "Qi's full brothers are sons of Ruoyou, who died in service to the throne. If Qi's brothers are punished with him, Ruoyou ought to be struck from the rolls, which would also be unjust."

sentences.zh: 宰相頗以為然，故誅锜詔下，唯止元惡一房而已。

translations.literal: The chancellors largely agreed, and therefore when the edict punishing Qi was issued, only the household of the chief culprit was affected.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors largely agreed, and when the edict punishing Qi was issued, only the household of the chief culprit was affected.

sentences.zh: 李峘，太宗第三子吳王恪之孫。

translations.literal: Li Huan was a grandson of Prince Wu Li Ke, the third son of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan was a grandson of Prince Wu Li Ke, the third son of Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 恪第三子琨生信安王祎，祎生三子：峘、嶧、峴。

translations.literal: Ke's third son Kun fathered Prince Xin'an Li Yi; Yi had three sons: Huan, Yi, and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's third son Kun fathered Prince Xin'an Li Yi, who had three sons: Huan, Yi, and Xian.

sentences.zh: 峘誌行修立，天寶中為南宮郎，歷典諸曹十余年。

translations.literal: Huan's conduct and will were cultivated and upright; in the Tianbao era he was an official of the Southern Palace and for more than ten years held charge of various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was upright in conduct and purpose; in Tianbao he served in the Southern Palace and for more than ten years held charge of various bureaus.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，哀毀得禮，服闋，以郡王子例封趙國公。

translations.literal: When in mourning for his father his grief was fitting to ritual; when mourning ended, by the precedent for sons of princes of commanderies he was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his father he observed the rites with fitting grief; when mourning ended he was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao by the precedent for sons of commandery princes.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠秉政，郎官不附己者悉出於外，峘自考功郎中出為睢陽太守。

translations.literal: When Yang Guozhong held power, all court officials who did not attach themselves to him were sent out of the capital; Huan was transferred from director in the Ministry of Honors to prefect of Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guozhong held power, court officials who did not support him were sent out of the capital; Huan was transferred from director in the Ministry of Honors to prefect of Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 尋而弟峴出為魏郡太守，兄弟夾河典郡，皆以理行稱。

translations.literal: Soon his younger brother Xian went out as prefect of Wei Commandery; the brothers governed prefectures on opposite banks of the river and were both praised for orderly rule.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his younger brother Xian became prefect of Wei commandery; the brothers governed prefectures on opposite banks of the Yellow River and were both praised for good government.

sentences.zh: 十四載，入計京師。

translations.literal: In year 14 he entered the capital to report accounts.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he went to the capital to report accounts.

sentences.zh: 屬祿山之亂，玄宗幸蜀，峘奔赴行在，除武部侍郎，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Lushan's rebellion broke out, Xuanzong went to Shu; Huan hurried to the imperial headquarters and was made Vice Minister of War and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled and Xuanzong went to Shu, Huan hurried to the imperial headquarters and was made Vice Minister of War and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 俄拜蜀郡太守、劍南節度采訪使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Shu Commandery and investigation commissioner of the Jiannan military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Shu commandery and investigation commissioner of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 上皇在成都，健兒郭千仞夜謀亂，上皇禦玄英樓招諭，不從，峘與六軍兵馬使陳玄禮等平之，以功加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Retired Emperor was at Chengdu, the strongman Guo Qianren plotted rebellion by night; the Retired Emperor mounted the Tower of Mysterious Glory to summon and instruct them, but they would not obey. Huan, with the Six Armies horse-and-chariot commissioner Chen Xuanli and others, quelled it; for his merit he was given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal.
translations.idiomatic: When the retired emperor was at Chengdu, the strongman Guo Qianren plotted a night revolt; the retired emperor mounted the Tower of Mysterious Glory to summon and instruct them, but they refused. Huan, with Chen Xuanli of the Six Armies and others, put down the revolt and was given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal for his merit.

sentences.zh: 時峴為鳳翔太守，匡翊肅宗，兄弟俱效勛力。

translations.literal: At that time Xian was prefect of Fengxiang, supporting and assisting Suzong; the brothers both rendered meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xian was prefect of Fengxiang, supporting Suzong; both brothers rendered distinguished service.

sentences.zh: 從上皇還京，為戶部尚書，峴為御史大夫，兼京兆尹，封梁國公。

translations.literal: When they followed the Retired Emperor back to the capital, Huan became Minister of Revenue; Xian became Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When they followed the retired emperor back to the capital, Huan became Minister of Revenue; Xian became censor-in-chief and metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同制封公。

translations.literal: The brothers were enfeoffed as dukes by the same edict.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were enfeoffed as dukes in the same edict.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，兼御史大夫，持節都統淮南、江南、江西節度、宣慰、觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan he was concurrently Censor-in-Chief and, bearing credentials, overall commander of the Huainan, Jiangnan, and Jiangxi military commissions and pacification, consolation, observation, and disposal commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyuan he was concurrently censor-in-chief and, with credentials, overall commander of the Huainan, Jiangnan, and Jiangxi commissions and pacification, consolation, observation, and disposal commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年，以宋州刺史劉展握兵河南，有異志，乃陽拜展淮南節度使，而密詔揚州長史鄧景山與峘圖之。

translations.literal: In year 2, because the prefect of Songzhou Liu Zhan held troops in Henan and harbored disloyal intent, he was openly appointed military commissioner of Huainan while a secret edict ordered Yangzhou chief administrator Deng Jingshan and Huan to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, because Liu Zhan of Songzhou held troops in Henan and harbored disloyal intent, he was openly appointed Huainan commissioner while a secret edict ordered Deng Jingshan of Yangzhou and Huan to plot against him.

sentences.zh: 時展徒黨方強，既受詔，即以兵渡淮。

translations.literal: At that time Zhan's faction was still strong; once he received the appointment he immediately crossed the Huai with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's faction was still strong; once he received the appointment he immediately crossed the Huai with troops.

sentences.zh: 景山、峘拒之壽春，為展所敗。

translations.literal: Jingshan and Huan resisted him at Shouchun and were defeated by Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan and Huan resisted him at Shouchun and were defeated.

sentences.zh: 峘走渡江，保丹陽，坐貶袁州司馬。

translations.literal: Huan fled across the river and held Danyang; he was demoted to military aide of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huan fled across the river and held Danyang; he was demoted to military aide of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年，病卒於貶所，追贈揚州大都督，官給遞乘，護柩還京。

translations.literal: In Baoying year 2 he died of illness at his place of exile; posthumously he was made Grand Protector-General of Yangzhou, and official relay transport was provided to escort his coffin back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying 2 he died of illness in exile and was posthumously made Grand Protector-General of Yangzhou; official relay transport was provided to escort his coffin back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，峘為戶部尚書，峴為吏部尚書、知政事，嶧為戶部侍郎、銀青光祿大夫，兄弟同居長興裏第，門列三戟，兩國公門十六戟，一、三品門十二戟，榮耀冠時。

translations.literal: Earlier Huan was Minister of Revenue, Xian was Minister of Personnel and handled state affairs, and Yi was Vice Minister of Revenue and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal; the brothers lived together in the Changxing Lane residence, with three halberds at the gate—the gate of two dukes bore sixteen halberds, that of first- and third-rank officials twelve—and their glory surpassed all of their time.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of their glory Huan was Minister of Revenue, Xian Minister of Personnel and chief minister, and Yi Vice Minister of Revenue; the brothers lived together in the Changxing Lane residence with three halberds at the gate—sixteen for a ducal household, twelve for first- and third-rank officials—and their splendor surpassed all their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 嶧位終蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: Yi ended his career as prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi ended his career as prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 峴，樂善下士，少有吏幹。

translations.literal: Xian delighted in goodness and treated scholars generously; from youth he had administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Xian delighted in doing good and treated scholars generously; from youth he showed administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 以門廕入仕，累遷高陵令，政術知名。

translations.literal: Through family privilege he entered office and was repeatedly promoted to magistrate of Gaoling, becoming known for his governing skill.
translations.idiomatic: Through family privilege he entered office and rose to magistrate of Gaoling, where he became known for his governing skill.

sentences.zh: 特遷萬年令、河南少尹、魏郡太守；

translations.literal: He was specially promoted to magistrate of Wannian, Vice Governor of Henan, and prefect of Wei Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to magistrate of Wannian, vice governor of Henan, and prefect of Wei commandery;

sentences.zh: 入為金吾將軍，遷將作監，改京兆府尹，所在皆著聲績。

translations.literal: he entered the capital as General of the Golden Guards, was transferred to Director of Palace Buildings, and was changed to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao; wherever he served he won reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: he entered the capital as general of the golden guards, became director of palace buildings, and was made metropolitan governor of Jingzhao; wherever he served he won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載，連雨六十余日，宰臣楊國忠惡其不附己，以雨災歸咎京兆尹，乃出為長沙郡太守。

translations.literal: In Tianbao year 13 rain fell for more than sixty days in succession; the chief minister Yang Guozhong disliked him for not attaching himself to him and blamed the metropolitan governor for the rain disaster, sending him out as prefect of Changsha Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 13 it rained for more than sixty days; Chief Minister Yang Guozhong, who disliked him for not supporting him, blamed the metropolitan governor for the rain disaster and sent him out as prefect of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 時京師米麥踴貴，百姓謠曰：「欲得米粟賤，無過追李峴。」

translations.literal: At that time grain and wheat in the capital soared in price; the people sang: If you want rice and grain cheap, nothing surpasses recalling Li Xian."
translations.idiomatic: Grain prices in the capital soared, and the people sang: "If you want rice and grain cheap, nothing beats recalling Li Xian."

sentences.zh: 其為政得人心如此。

translations.literal: Such was the hold his government had on people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the hold his government had on the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 至德初，朝廷務收才傑，以清寇難，峴召至行在，拜扶風太守、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide the court strove to gather outstanding talent to clear away banditry; Xian was summoned to the headquarters and made prefect of Fufeng and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhide the court sought outstanding talent to quell rebellion; Xian was summoned to headquarters and made prefect of Fufeng and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 至德二年十二月，制曰：「銀青光祿大夫、守禮部尚書李峴，饋軍周給，開物成務。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of Zhide year 2 an edict said: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Acting Minister of Rites Li Xian has supplied the army comprehensively and opened affairs to completion.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Zhide 2 an edict declared: "Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and acting Minister of Rites Li Xian has supplied the army fully and brought affairs to completion.

sentences.zh: 可光祿大夫，行御史大夫，兼京兆尹，封梁國公。」

translations.literal: He may be made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Censor-in-Chief, and concurrently Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting censor-in-chief, and metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang."

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，制曰：「李峴朝廷碩德，宗室藎臣。

translations.literal: In Qianyuan year 2 an edict said: Li Xian is a great pillar of the court and a loyal minister of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 2 an edict declared: "Li Xian is a great pillar of the court and a loyal minister of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 可中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。」

translations.literal: He may be made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and associate chief minister."

sentences.zh: 與呂諲、李揆、第五锜同拜相。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief minister together with Lü Yin, Li Kui, and Diwu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief minister together with Lü Yin, Li Kui, and Diwu Qi.

sentences.zh: 峴位望稍高，軍國大事，諸公莫敢言，皆獨決於峴，由是諲等銜之。

translations.literal: Xian's standing was somewhat higher; on great matters of army and state the others dared not speak and left decisions to Xian alone, and therefore Yin and the rest harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's standing was somewhat higher; on great matters of army and state the others dared not speak and left decisions to Xian alone, and Yin and the rest resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 初，李輔國判行軍司馬，潛令官軍於人間聽察是非，謂之察事。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Fuguo had served as acting campaigning deputy and secretly ordered army officers to listen among the people for right and wrong, calling this investigation duty.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Fuguo had served as acting campaigning deputy and secretly ordered army officers to spy among the people, calling this investigation duty.

sentences.zh: 忠良被誣構者繼有之，須有追呼，諸司莫敢抗。

translations.literal: Loyal men were framed in succession; whenever summons came, no office dared resist.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal men were framed one after another; whenever summons came, no office dared resist.

sentences.zh: 御史臺、大理寺重囚在獄，推斷未了，牒追就銀臺，不問輕重，一時釋放，莫敢違者。

translations.literal: Heavy prisoners in the Censorate and Court of Judicial Review, whose cases were not yet concluded, were summoned by document to the Silver Terrace; without regard to severity they were all released at once, and none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy prisoners in the Censorate and Court of Judicial Review whose cases were unfinished were summoned to the Silver Terrace and released at once without regard to severity, and none dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 每日於銀臺門決天下事，須處分，便稱制敕，禁中符印，悉佩之出入。

translations.literal: Each day at the Silver Terrace Gate he decided affairs of the realm; whenever disposition was needed he called it an edict, and he wore all the palace seals in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Each day at the Silver Terrace Gate he decided affairs of the realm; whenever action was needed he called it an edict, and he carried all the palace seals in and out.

sentences.zh: 縱有敕，輔國押署，然後施行。

translations.literal: Even when there was an edict, Fuguo had to countersign before it could be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Even when an edict existed, Fuguo had to countersign before it could be carried out.

sentences.zh: 及峴為相，叩頭論輔國專權亂國，上悟，賞峴正直，事並變革。

translations.literal: When Xian became chief minister he kowtowed and argued that Fuguo's monopoly of power was ruining the state; the emperor understood, rewarded Xian's uprightness, and all these practices were reformed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian became chief minister he kowtowed and argued that Fuguo's monopoly of power was ruining the state; the emperor understood, rewarded Xian's uprightness, and reformed all these practices.

sentences.zh: 輔國以此讓行軍司馬，請歸本官，察事等並停，由是深怨峴。

translations.literal: Fuguo therefore yielded the post of campaigning deputy and asked to return to his original office; investigation duty and the like were all stopped, and for this he deeply resented Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo therefore yielded the campaigning deputy post and asked to return to his original office; investigation duty and the like were stopped, and for this he deeply resented Xian.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔七馬坊押官，先頗為盜，劫掠平人，州縣不能制，天興縣令知捕賊謝夷甫擒獲決殺之。

translations.literal: A custodian of the Seven Horse Paddocks at Fengxiang had long been a robber, plundering common people, and prefectures and counties could not control him; the magistrate of Tianxing, Xie Yifu, who was charged with catching bandits, seized and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: A custodian of the Seven Horse Paddocks at Fengxiang had long been a robber who plundered common people beyond the control of local officials; Xie Yifu, magistrate of Tianxing charged with catching bandits, seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: 其妻進狀訴夫冤。

translations.literal: His wife submitted a petition complaining of her husband's wrongful death.
translations.idiomatic: His wife submitted a petition claiming her husband had been wrongfully killed.

sentences.zh: 輔國先為飛龍使，黨其人，為之上訴，詔監察御史孫鎣推之。

translations.literal: Fuguo had formerly been commissioner of the Flying Dragon Office and was partisan to the man; he appealed on his behalf, and an edict ordered Investigating Censor Sun Jin to examine the case.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo had formerly headed the Flying Dragon Office and favored the man; he appealed on his behalf, and an edict ordered Investigating Censor Sun Jin to examine the case.

sentences.zh: 鎣初直其事。

translations.literal: Jin at first upheld the original judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Jin at first upheld the original judgment.

sentences.zh: 其妻又訴，詔令御史中丞崔伯陽、刑部侍郎李曄、大理卿權獻三司訊之，三司與鎣同。

translations.literal: The wife appealed again; an edict ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Boyang, Vice Minister of Justice Li Ye, and Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Quan Xian to examine the case jointly; the three offices agreed with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The wife appealed again; an edict ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Boyang, Vice Minister of Justice Li Ye, and Chief Judge Quan Xian to examine the case jointly; the three offices agreed with Jin.

sentences.zh: 妻論訴不已，詔令侍御史毛若虛覆之，若虛歸罪於夷甫，又言伯陽等有情，不能質定刑獄。

translations.literal: The wife kept appealing without end; an edict ordered Attending Censor Mao Ruoxu to review the case. Ruoxu placed guilt on Yifu and also said Boyang and the others were partial and could not settle criminal judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The wife kept appealing; an edict ordered Attending Censor Mao Ruoxu to review the case. Ruoxu blamed Yifu and said Boyang and the others were partial and could not settle the criminal judgment.

sentences.zh: 伯陽怒，使人召若虛，詞氣不順。

translations.literal: Boyang was angry and sent someone to summon Ruoxu; his tone was not respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Boyang was angry and sent for Ruoxu; his tone was disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 伯陽欲上言之，若虛先馳謁，告急於肅宗，云：「已知，卿出去。」

translations.literal: Boyang wished to report this to the throne; Ruoxu hurried ahead to an audience and appealed in urgency to Suzong, saying: I understand; you may go out."
translations.idiomatic: Boyang wished to report this to the throne; Ruoxu hurried ahead to an audience and appealed urgently to Suzong, saying: "I understand; you may go out."

sentences.zh: 若虛奏曰：「臣出即死。」

translations.literal: Ruoxu memorialized: If I go out I shall die at once."
translations.idiomatic: Ruoxu memorialized: "If I go out I shall die at once."

sentences.zh: 上因留在簾內。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore kept him inside the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore kept him inside the curtain.

sentences.zh: 有頃，伯陽至，上問之，伯陽頗言若虛順旨，附會中人。

translations.literal: After a while Boyang arrived; the emperor questioned him, and Boyang spoke at length of how Ruoxu followed the imperial will and curried favor with the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: After a while Boyang arrived; the emperor questioned him, and Boyang said at length that Ruoxu followed the imperial will and curried favor with the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 上怒，叱出之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and shouted him out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and shouted him out.

sentences.zh: 伯陽貶端州高要尉，權獻郴州桂陽尉，鳳翔尹嚴向及李曄皆貶嶺下一尉，鎣除名長流播州。

translations.literal: Boyang was demoted to military aide of Gaoyao in Duanzhou; Quan Xian to military aide of Guiyang in Chenzhou; the Fengxiang governor Yan Xiang and Li Ye were both demoted to military aides south of the ranges; Jin was struck from the rolls and exiled far to Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Boyang was demoted to military aide of Gaoyao in Duanzhou; Quan Xian to military aide of Guiyang in Chenzhou; the Fengxiang governor Yan Xiang and Li Ye were both demoted to military aides south of the ranges; Jin was struck from the rolls and exiled to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 峴以數人鹹非其罪，所責太重，欲理之，遂奏：「若虛希旨用刑，不守國法，陛下若信之重輕，是無御史臺。」

translations.literal: Xian considered that several men were none of them guilty and that the penalties were too heavy; wishing to set matters right, he memorialized: Ruoxu applied punishment to please the throne and did not keep to state law; if Your Majesty trusts his judgment of severity, that is to abolish the Censorate."
translations.idiomatic: Xian considered that several men were innocent and that the penalties were too heavy; wishing to set matters right, he memorialized: "Ruoxu applied punishment to please the throne and did not keep to state law; if Your Majesty trusts his judgment of severity, that is to abolish the Censorate."

sentences.zh: 上怒峴言，出峴為蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry at Xian's words and sent him out as prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry at Xian's words and sent him out as prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 時右散騎常侍韓擇木入對，上謂之曰：「峴欲專權耶？

translations.literal: At that time the Right Regular Attendant Han Zemu entered for audience; the emperor said to him: Does Xian wish to monopolize power?
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Right Regular Attendant Han Zemu entered for audience; the emperor said to him: "Does Xian wish to monopolize power?

sentences.zh: 何乃雲任毛若虛是無御史臺也？

translations.literal: Why does he say that trusting Mao Ruoxu is to have no Censorate?
translations.idiomatic: Why does he say that trusting Mao Ruoxu is to have no Censorate?

sentences.zh: 令貶蜀州刺史，朕自覺用法太寬。」

translations.literal: I ordered him demoted to prefect of Shuzhou; I myself feel my application of the law was too lenient."
