translations.idiomatic: I ordered him demoted to prefect of Shu; I myself feel my application of the law was too lenient."

sentences.zh: 擇木對曰：「峴言直，非專權。

translations.literal: Zemu replied: Xian's words are straightforward, not a bid for monopoly of power.
translations.idiomatic: Zemu replied: "Xian spoke plainly; he was not seeking to monopolize power.

sentences.zh: 陛下寬之，祗益聖德爾。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty is lenient with him, that will only add to your sacred virtue."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty is lenient with him, that will only add to your sacred virtue."

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，征峴為荊南節度、江陵尹，知江淮選補使。

translations.literal: When Daizong took the throne, Xian was summoned as military commissioner of Jingnan and metropolitan governor of Jiangling, and as commissioner for selection and appointment in Jiang-Huai.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong took the throne, Xian was summoned as military commissioner of Jingnan and metropolitan governor of Jiangling, and as commissioner for appointments in Jiang-Huai.

sentences.zh: 入為禮部尚書，兼宗正卿。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of Rites and concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Minister of Rites and concurrently director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 屬鑾輿幸陜，峴由商山路赴行在。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went to Shan, Xian traveled by the Shangshan road to the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Shan, Xian traveled by the Shangshan road to join the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 既還京師，拜峴為黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: After the return to the capital he was made Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After the return to the capital he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 故事，宰臣不於政事堂邀客，時海內多務，宰相元載等見中官傳詔命至中書者，引之升政事堂，仍置榻待之；

translations.literal: By precedent chief ministers did not receive guests in the Hall of Administration; at that time affairs within the seas were many, and when the chancellor Yuan Zai and others saw eunuchs come to the Secretariat bearing edicts, they would lead them up into the Hall of Administration and still set out couches to receive them;
translations.idiomatic: By precedent chief ministers did not receive guests in the Hall of Administration; at that time the realm was overwhelmed with business, and when Chancellor Yuan Zai and others saw eunuchs come to the Secretariat bearing edicts, they would lead them into the Hall of Administration and set out couches for them;

sentences.zh: 峴為宰相，令去其榻。

translations.literal: when Xian became chief minister he ordered the couches removed.
translations.idiomatic: when Xian became chief minister he ordered the couches removed.

sentences.zh: 奏請常參官各舉堪任諫官、憲官者，不限人數。

translations.literal: He memorialized that each official in regular attendance should recommend men fit to serve as remonstrating officials or censorial officials, with no limit on number.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that each official in regular attendance should recommend men fit to serve as remonstrating or censorial officials, with no limit on number.

sentences.zh: 初收東京，受偽官陳希烈已下數百人，崔器希旨深刻，奏皆處死；

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was first recovered, several hundred false officials including Chen Xilie were taken; Cui Qi, seeking to please the throne with harsh severity, memorialized that all be put to death;
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital was first recovered, several hundred collaborators including Chen Xilie were taken; Cui Qi, seeking to please the throne with harsh severity, memorialized that all be put to death;

sentences.zh: 上意亦欲懲勸天下，欲從器議。

translations.literal: the emperor also wished to warn and instruct the realm and intended to follow Qi's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor also wished to warn the realm and intended to follow Qi's proposal.

sentences.zh: 時峴為三司使，執之曰：「夫事有首從，情有輕重，若一概處死，恐非陛下含弘之義，又失國家惟新之典。

translations.literal: At that time Xian was commissioner of the Three Offices; he held fast and said: Affairs have leaders and followers, circumstances have light and heavy weight; if all are put to death alike, I fear that is not Your Majesty's meaning of inclusive magnanimity, and it also loses the state's charter of renewal.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xian was commissioner of the Three Offices; he objected: "Affairs have leaders and followers, and circumstances vary in severity; if all are put to death alike, that is not Your Majesty's inclusive magnanimity, and it loses the state's charter of renewal.

sentences.zh: 且羯胡亂常，無不淩據，二京全陷，萬乘南巡，各顧其生，衣冠蕩覆。

translations.literal: Moreover the Jie barbarians threw the norms into disorder and none failed to overrun and seize; both capitals fell entirely, the imperial carriage toured south, each man looked to his own life, and the gentry were swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the rebels threw the norms into disorder; both capitals fell, the emperor went south, each man looked to his own survival, and the gentry were swept away.

sentences.zh: 或陛下親戚，或勛舊子孫，皆置極法，恐乖仁恕之旨。

translations.literal: Some are Your Majesty's kin, some are sons and grandsons of meritorious ministers—if all are subjected to the extreme penalty, I fear that strays from the purpose of benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Some are Your Majesty's kin, some are sons and grandsons of meritorious ministers—if all receive the extreme penalty, that strays from benevolence and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 昔者明王用刑，殲厥渠魁，脅從罔理。

translations.literal: Of old enlightened kings applied punishments by destroying the ringleaders and not reasoning with those coerced to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Of old enlightened kings punished by destroying the ringleaders and not holding those coerced to follow to the same account.

sentences.zh: 況河北殘寇未平，官吏多陷，茍容漏網，適開自新之路，若盡行誅，是堅叛逆之黨，誰人更圖效順？

translations.literal: Moreover bandits remain in Hebei, and many officials are implicated; if some are allowed to slip through the net, that opens the road to renewal—if all are executed, that hardens the party of rebellion; who will then plan to submit in loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover bandits remain in Hebei and many officials are implicated; if some are allowed to slip through, that opens the road to renewal—if all are executed, that hardens the rebels; who will then submit in loyalty?

sentences.zh: 困獸猶鬥，況數萬人乎！」

translations.literal: A cornered beast still fights—how much more tens of thousands of men!"
translations.idiomatic: A cornered beast still fights—how much more tens of thousands of men!"

sentences.zh: 崔器、呂諲，皆守文之吏，不識大體，殊無變通。

translations.literal: Cui Qi and Lü Yin were both officials who clung to the letter of the law, did not understand the larger pattern, and were wholly without flexibility.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qi and Lü Yin were both officials who clung to the letter of the law, did not understand the larger pattern, and were wholly inflexible.

sentences.zh: 廷議數日，方從峴奏，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Court debate lasted several days before Xian's memorial was followed, and very many were spared alive.
translations.idiomatic: Court debate lasted several days before Xian's memorial was followed, and very many lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 其料敵決事皆此類。

translations.literal: His assessment of enemies and decision of affairs were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His assessment of enemies and decision of affairs were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 竟為中官所擠，罷知政事，為太子詹事，尋遷吏部尚書，知江淮舉選，置銓洪州。

translations.literal: In the end he was squeezed out by eunuchs, ceased handling state affairs, became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and soon was transferred to Minister of Personnel, in charge of selection in Jiang-Huai, with the board of appointment set at Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was squeezed out by eunuchs, left the chief ministry, became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and soon became Minister of Personnel in charge of selection in Jiang-Huai, with the appointment board at Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，改檢校兵部尚書，兼衢州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to irregularly appointed Minister of War and concurrently prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made irregular Minister of War and concurrently prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年七月以疾終，時年五十八。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Yongtai year 2 he died of illness, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the seventh month of Yongtai 2, at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 李巨，曾祖父虢王鳳，高祖之第十四子也。

translations.literal: Li Ju's great-grandfather was Prince Guo Li Feng, the fourteenth son of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju's great-grandfather was Prince Guo Li Feng, the fourteenth son of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 鳳孫邕，嗣虢王，巨即邕之第二子也。

translations.literal: Feng's grandson Yong succeeded to the title Prince Guo; Ju was Yong's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's grandson Yong succeeded as Prince Guo; Ju was Yong's second son.

sentences.zh: 剛銳果決，頗涉獵書史，好屬文。

translations.literal: He was firm, sharp, and resolute, dipped considerably into books and histories, and loved literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was firm, sharp, and resolute, read widely in books and histories, and loved literary composition.

sentences.zh: 開元中為嗣虢王。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he was heir to Prince Guo.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era he was heir to Prince Guo.

sentences.zh: 天寶五載，出為西河太守。

translations.literal: In Tianbao year 5 he went out as prefect of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 5 he went out as prefect of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 皇太子杜良娣之妹婿柳勣陷詔獄，巨母扶余氏，吉溫嫡母之妹也，溫為京兆士曹，推勣之黨，以徐征等往來巨家，資給之，由是坐貶義陽郡司馬。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince's brother-in-law Liu Ji, husband of the younger sister of Consort Du Liangdi, was caught in an imperial prison case. Ju's mother was of the Fu clan, a younger sister of Ji Wen's stepmother's family; Wen was a clerk in Jingzhao and pursued Ji's associates, finding that Xu Zheng and others had frequented Ju's household and supplied him—for this Ju was demoted to military aide of Yiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, husband of the younger sister of Consort Du Liangdi, was caught in an imperial prison case. Ju's mother was of the Fu clan, related to Ji Wen's stepmother; Wen, a Jingzhao clerk, pursued Ji's associates and found that Xu Zheng and others had frequented Ju's household and supplied him—for this Ju was demoted to military aide of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 六載，御史中丞楊慎矜為李林甫、王鉷構陷得罪，其黨史敬忠亦伏法。

translations.literal: In year 6 Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Shenjin was framed and ruined by Li Linfu and Wang Hong; his associate Shi Jingzhong also suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Shenjin was framed and ruined by Li Linfu and Wang Hong; his associate Shi Jingzhong was also executed.

sentences.zh: 以巨與敬忠相識，坐解官，於南賓郡安置。

translations.literal: Because Ju knew Jingzhong, he was dismissed from office and placed under restraint in Nanbin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ju knew Jingzhong, he was dismissed from office and placed under restraint in Nanbin.

sentences.zh: 又起為夷陵郡太守。

translations.literal: He was later recalled as prefect of Yiling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as prefect of Yiling.

sentences.zh: 及祿山陷東京，玄宗方擇將帥，張垍言巨善騎射，有謀略，玄宗追至京師。

translations.literal: When Lushan took the Eastern Capital, Xuanzong was choosing generals; Zhang Kai said Ju was skilled at riding and archery and had strategy, and Xuanzong summoned him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan took the Eastern Capital, Xuanzong was choosing generals; Zhang Kai said Ju was skilled at riding and archery and had strategic ability, and Xuanzong summoned him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠素與巨相識，忌之，謂人曰：「如此小兒，豈得令見人主！」

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong had long known Ju and was jealous of him; he said to others: Such a stripling—how can he be allowed to see the sovereign!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong had long known Ju and was jealous; he said to others: "Such a stripling—how can he be allowed to see the sovereign!"

sentences.zh: 經月余日不得見。

translations.literal: For more than a month he was not granted an audience.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a month he was not granted an audience.

sentences.zh: 玄宗使中官召入奏事，玄宗大悅，遂令中官劉奉庭宣敕令宰相與巨語，幾亭午，方出。

translations.literal: Xuanzong had a eunuch summon him to report; Xuanzong was greatly pleased and then had the eunuch Liu Fengting proclaim an edict ordering the chief ministers to speak with Ju; it was nearly noon before he came out.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had a eunuch summon him to report; the emperor was greatly pleased and had the eunuch Liu Fengting proclaim an edict ordering the chief ministers to speak with Ju; it was nearly noon before he emerged.

sentences.zh: 國忠頗怠，對奉庭謂巨曰：「比來人多口打賊，公不爾乎？」

translations.literal: Guozhong was rather indifferent; facing Fengting he said to Ju: Lately many men only talk of fighting the rebels with their mouths—are you not like that?"
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was rather indifferent; facing Fengting he said to Ju: "Lately many men only talk of fighting the rebels—are you not like that?"

sentences.zh: 巨曰：「不知若個軍將能與相公手打賊乎？」

translations.literal: Ju said: I wonder which army officer can fight the rebels hand to hand with the Chancellor?"
translations.idiomatic: Ju said: "I wonder which army officer can fight the rebels hand to hand with the Chancellor?"

sentences.zh: 尋授陳留譙郡太守、攝御史大夫、河南節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Chenliu and Qiao commanderies, acting Censor-in-Chief, and military commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Chenliu and Qiao, acting censor-in-chief, and military commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 翌日，巨稱官銜奉謝，玄宗驚曰：「何得令攝？」

translations.literal: The next day Ju gave thanks under his title; Xuanzong was startled and said: How could he be made acting?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ju gave thanks under his title; Xuanzong was startled and said: "How could he be made acting?"

sentences.zh: 即日詔兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: That same day an edict made him Censor-in-Chief concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an edict made him censor-in-chief concurrently.

sentences.zh: 巨奏曰：「方今艱難，恐為賊所詐，如忽召臣，不知何以取信？」

translations.literal: Ju memorialized: In present hardship I fear being deceived by rebels; if I am suddenly summoned, how will trust be established?"
translations.idiomatic: Ju memorialized: "In present hardship I fear being deceived by rebels; if I am suddenly summoned, how will trust be established?"

sentences.zh: 玄宗劈木契分授之，遂以臣兼統嶺南節度使何履光、黔中節度使趙國珍、南陽節度使魯炅，先領三節度事。

translations.literal: Xuanzong split a wooden tally and gave him a portion; Ju was thus made to command concurrently the Lingnan military commissioner He Luguang, the Qianzhong military commissioner Zhao Guozhen, and the Nanyang military commissioner Lu Hui, first taking charge of the three commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong split a wooden tally and gave him a portion; Ju was thus placed in concurrent command of the Lingnan commissioner He Luguang, the Qianzhong commissioner Zhao Guozhen, and the Nanyang commissioner Lu Hui, first taking charge of all three commissions.

sentences.zh: 有詔貶炅為果毅，以潁川太守來瑱兼御史中丞代之。

translations.literal: An edict demoted Hui to garrison officer and sent the Yingchuan prefect Lai Tian, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demoted Hui to garrison officer and sent the Yingchuan prefect Lai Tian, concurrently vice censor-in-chief, to replace him.

sentences.zh: 巨奏曰：「若炅能存孤城，其功足以補過，則何以處之？」

translations.literal: Ju memorialized: If Hui can hold the isolated city and his merit is enough to offset his fault, how then should he be treated?"
translations.idiomatic: Ju memorialized: "If Hui can hold the isolated city and his merit is enough to offset his fault, how then should he be treated?"

sentences.zh: 玄宗曰：「卿隨宜處置之。」

translations.literal: Xuanzong said: Handle it as you see fit."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong said: "Handle it as you see fit."

sentences.zh: 巨至內鄉，趣南陽，賊將畢思琛聞之，解圍走。

translations.literal: When Ju reached Neixiang and hurried to Nanyang, the rebel general Bi Sichen heard of it and lifted the siege and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Ju reached Neixiang and hurried to Nanyang, the rebel general Bi Sichen heard of it and lifted the siege and fled.

sentences.zh: 巨趣何履光、趙國珍同至南陽，宣敕貶炅，削其章服，令隨軍效力。

translations.literal: Ju urged He Luguang and Zhao Guozhen to come together to Nanyang, proclaimed the edict demoting Hui, stripped him of insignia and robes, and ordered him to serve with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Ju urged He Luguang and Zhao Guozhen to come to Nanyang together, proclaimed the edict demoting Hui, stripped him of insignia and robes, and ordered him to serve with the army.

sentences.zh: 至日晚，以恩命令炅復位。

translations.literal: By evening, by grace he ordered Hui restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: By evening, by grace he ordered Hui restored to office.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，為太子少傅。

translations.literal: In Zhide year 2 he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 2 he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十月，收西京，為留守、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Western Capital was recovered; he served as defender and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Western Capital was recovered; he served as defender and concurrently censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 三年夏四月，加太子少師、兼河南尹，充東京留守，判尚書省事，充東畿采訪等使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer of year 3 he was given the added posts of Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Metropolitan Governor of Henan, served as defender of the Eastern Capital, judged affairs of the Department of State Affairs, and was made investigation commissioner of the Eastern Capital region and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer of year 3 he was given the added posts of Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and metropolitan governor of Henan, served as defender of the Eastern Capital, judged Secretariat affairs, and was made investigation commissioner of the Eastern Capital region.

sentences.zh: 於城市橋梁稅出入車牛等錢以供國用，頗有幹沒，士庶怨讟。

translations.literal: He levied taxes on carts, oxen, and the like entering and leaving at city gates and bridges to supply state use; there was considerable embezzlement, and gentry and commoners resented and denounced him.
translations.idiomatic: He levied taxes on carts and oxen entering and leaving at city gates and bridges to supply state revenue; there was considerable embezzlement, and gentry and commoners resented and denounced him.

sentences.zh: 後與妃張氏不睦，張氏即皇后從父妹也。

translations.literal: Later he was on bad terms with his consort Lady Zhang, who was the empress's cousin on her father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was on bad terms with his consort Lady Zhang, who was the empress's cousin on her father's side.

sentences.zh: 宗正卿李遵構之，發其所犯贓賄，貶為遂州刺史。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Clan Court Li Zun framed him, exposed his bribery and corruption, and had him demoted to prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the Imperial Clan Court Li Zun framed him, exposed his bribery and corruption, and had him demoted to prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 屬劍南東川節度兵馬使、梓州刺史段子璋反，以眾襲節度使李奐於綿州，路經遂州，巨蒼黃修屬郡禮迎之，為子璋所殺。

translations.literal: It happened that the Jiannan East River military aide and prefect of Zizhou Duan Zizhang rebelled, led troops to attack the military commissioner Li Huan at Mianzhou, passed through Suizhou on the way, and Ju, in haste, had the subordinate prefecture prepare ritual to welcome him—whereupon he was killed by Zizhang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiannan East River military aide and prefect of Zizhou Duan Zizhang rebelled, led troops to attack Commissioner Li Huan at Mianzhou, and passed through Suizhou, Ju hurriedly had the subordinate prefecture prepare ritual to welcome him—and was killed by Zizhang.

sentences.zh: 子則之，以宗室歷官，好學，年五十余，每執經詣太學聽受。

translations.literal: His son Zezhi, through the imperial clan rising in office, loved learning; in his fifties he still carried the classics to the Imperial Academy to listen and receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zezhi, rising through the imperial clan, loved learning; in his fifties he still carried the classics to the Imperial Academy to attend lectures.

sentences.zh: 嗣曹王臯自荊南來朝，稱薦之，貞元二年，自睦王府長史遷左金吾衛大將軍，以從父甥竇申追遊無閑親累，貶昭州司馬。

translations.literal: Prince Si Cao Li Gao came to court from Jingnan and praised and recommended him; in Zhenyuan year 2 he was transferred from chief administrator of the Prince of Mu's establishment to General of the Left Golden Guards; because his cousin on his father's side Dou Shen pursued pleasure without restraint and implicated kin, he was demoted to military aide of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Si Cao Li Gao came to court from Jingnan and recommended him; in Zhenyuan 2 he rose from chief administrator of the Prince of Mu's establishment to General of the Left Golden Guards; because his cousin Dou Shen pursued pleasure without restraint and implicated kin, he was demoted to military aide of Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：暠孝友清慎，居官有稱；

translations.literal: The historian says: Gao was filial, friendly, pure, and cautious, and won praise in office;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Gao was filial, friendly, pure, and cautious, and won praise in office;

sentences.zh: 齊物貞廉整肅，復節制權謀；

translations.literal: Qi Wu was upright, incorrupt, stern, and orderly; Fu exercised restraint and strategic calculation;
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wu was upright, incorrupt, stern, and orderly; Fu exercised restraint and strategic calculation;

sentences.zh: 國貞清白守法，皆神通之曾玄，宗室之翹楚。

translations.literal: Guozhen was pure, white, and law-abiding—all were great-great-grandsons or great-grandsons of Shentong, outstanding men of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen was pure and law-abiding—all were descendants of Shentong, outstanding men of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 锜之為逆，不累其親，前人之積德彰矣，當朝之用法明矣。

translations.literal: Qi's rebellion did not implicate his kin; the accumulated virtue of forebears was manifest, and the present court's application of law was clear.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's rebellion did not implicate his kin; the accumulated virtue of forebears was manifest, and the present court's application of law was clear.

sentences.zh: 然暠發人陰私，齊物積財興議，國貞急於操下，皆尺之短也。

translations.literal: Yet Gao exposed people's private affairs, Qi Wu amassed wealth and stirred debate, and Guozhen was harsh in controlling subordinates—these were all foot-long flaws.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gao exposed people's private affairs, Qi Wu amassed wealth and stirred debate, and Guozhen was harsh toward subordinates—these were all flaws in the foot-long measure.

sentences.zh: 麟修整，峘循良，匪躬立事，始終無玷者，皆宗室之英也。

translations.literal: Lin was well ordered, Huan was orderly and good; those who devoted themselves to affairs without stain from beginning to end were all heroes of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was well ordered, Huan was orderly and good; those who devoted themselves to affairs without stain from beginning to end were all heroes of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 峴之剛正才略，有足可稱。

translations.literal: Xian's firm uprightness and talent in strategy were well worth praise.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's firm uprightness and strategic talent were well worth praise.

sentences.zh: 初為國忠所憎，終沮朝恩之勢。

translations.literal: At first he was hated by Guozhong; in the end the power of court favor was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was hated by Guozhong; in the end the power of court favor was blocked.

sentences.zh: 處群邪之內，堅獨正之心，是不吐也；

translations.literal: Standing among many evils with a heart alone upright—that is not to yield;
translations.idiomatic: Standing among many evils with a heart alone upright—that is not to yield;

sentences.zh: 活東都之命，是不茹也。

translations.literal: saving the lives of the Eastern Capital—that is not to swallow injustice.
translations.idiomatic: saving the lives of the Eastern Capital—that is not to swallow injustice.

sentences.zh: 庶幾乎仲山甫之道焉！

translations.literal: He may be compared to the way of Zhong Shanfu!
translations.idiomatic: He may be compared to the way of Zhong Shanfu!

sentences.zh: 巨以剛銳果決，亦可嘉焉，終以贓賄貪殘，良可痛也。

translations.literal: Ju for his firmness, sharpness, and resolution was also praiseworthy, yet in the end for bribery, corruption, greed, and cruelty he is truly lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Ju for his firmness, sharpness, and resolution was also praiseworthy, yet in the end for bribery, corruption, greed, and cruelty he is truly lamentable.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：宗室賢良，枝葉茂盛。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The imperial clan was worthy and good; its branches and leaves flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: The imperial clan was worthy and good; its branches and leaves flourished.

sentences.zh: 最尤者誰？

translations.literal: Who was most outstanding?
translations.idiomatic: Who was most outstanding?

sentences.zh: 峴獨守正。

translations.literal: Xian alone upheld rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Xian alone upheld rectitude.
